topic.name: The Shell Method: Rotating a Region About the X-Axis

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=3y^2-y^3$ and the $y$-axis, as shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3y^2-y^3 &= 0 \\[3pt] y^2(3-y) &= 0 \end{align*}

The solutions are $y=0, \, 3.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=3.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{c}^{d} y f(y) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{3} y\left( 3y^2-y^3 \right) \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=5y^3-5y^4$ and the $y$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 5y^3-5y^4 &= 0 \\[3pt] 5y^3(1-y) &= 0 \end{align*}

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{c}^{d} y f(y) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1} y\left( 5y^3-5y^4 \right) \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 10\pi \int_{0}^{1} \left( y^4-y^5 \right) \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 10\pi \left( \int_{0}^{1} y^4 \:\textrm{d}y - \int_{0}^{1} y^5 \textrm{d}y \right) \\[5pt] &= 10\pi \left( \left.\dfrac{y^5}{5}\right|_{0}^{1} - \left.\dfrac{y^6}{6}\right|_{0}^{1} \right) \\[5pt] &= 10\pi \left( \left(\dfrac{1}{5}-0\right) - \left(\dfrac{1}{6}-0\right) \right) \\[5pt] &= 10\pi \left(\dfrac{1}{5}- \dfrac{1}{6} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{3} \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=-8+6y-y^2$ and the $y$-axis. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis?
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} -8+6y-y^2 &= 0 \\[3pt] y^2-6y+8 &= 0 \\[3pt] (y-2)(y-4) &= 0 \end{align*}

The solutions are $y=2$ and $y=4.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=2$ to $y=4.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{c}^{d} y f(y) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{2}^{4} y\left(-8+6y-y^2 \right) \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=y^2-5y^3$ and the $y$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} y^2-5y^3 &= 0 \\[3pt] y^2(1-5y) &= 0 \end{align*}

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=\dfrac 1 5 .$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\dfrac 1 5.$

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} V &= 2\pi \int_{c}^{d} y f(y) \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1/5} y\left( y^2-5y^3 \right) \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \int_{0}^{1/5} \left( y^3-5y^4 \right) \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= 2\pi \left( \left.\dfrac{y^4}{4}\right|_{0}^{1/5} - 5\cdot\left.\dfrac{y^5}{5}\right|_{0}^{1/5} \right) \\[5pt] &=2\pi \left( \dfrac{1}{4\cdot 5^4} - \dfrac{1}{5^5} \right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{2\pi}{5^4} \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{5} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2\pi}{20\cdot 5^4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{6\,250} \end{align*}
